author: Chao-Jen Huang (ephoton)
title: Chip Outline Definition
description: Defines the physical package outline, ball/pad grid layout, and pin assignments for IC chip outline drawings. Supports top-view and bottom-view, standard rectangular grids, and WLCSP alternating (staggered) ball patterns.

release.description: Release date of this configuration in YYYY/MM/DD format.

project.description: Project / package configuration identifier, e.g. BVK027.

package.description: Package definition. A project may have multiple packages with different device codes.

code.description: Device part number (product code) for this package, e.g. BV6808.

description.description: Human-readable description of this package configuration.

dimension.description: Physical dimensions of the package body and ball geometry.

unit.description: Unit for all dimension values in this section.

x.description: Package body width — horizontal dimension (same direction as columns).

y.description: Package body height — vertical dimension (same direction as rows).

pitch_x.description: Center-to-center ball spacing in the X direction (column direction).

pitch_y.description: Center-to-center ball spacing in the Y direction (row direction).

margin_x.description: Distance from the package body edge to the nearest ball center in the X direction.

margin_y.description: Distance from the package body edge to the nearest ball center in the Y direction.

pin_config.description: Pin grid configuration and ball-to-signal mapping.

columns.description: Number of ball columns (horizontal count, the X dimension).

rows.description: Number of ball rows (vertical count, the Y dimension).

top_view.description: If true, the layout is drawn as seen from the top (die side). Column order reads right-to-left for ball designators. Default false = bottom view (PCB side), column order reads left-to-right.

alternating_type.description:
Ball stagger pattern for non-rectangular WLCSP layouts.
  0 = Standard rectangular grid — all rows have `columns` balls at regular positions.
  1 = Odd rows (B, D, ...) are staggered right by 0.5×pitch_x; those rows have `columns-1` balls.
  2 = Even rows (A, C, ...) are staggered right by 0.5×pitch_x; those rows have `columns-1` balls.
  3 = Partial last row — balls only at odd column indices (0, 2, 4 ...) of the last row.
  4 = Partial last row — balls only at even column indices (1, 3, ...) of the last row.
For types 1-2, use null in pin_map to visually represent the stagger offset. For types 3-4, use null for absent ball positions.

pin_map.description:
2D ball-to-signal map. Each element of the outer array is one row of balls (row A at index 0, row B at index 1, ...). Each element of the inner array is one column position. A string value is the signal name of the ball at that position. A null value means no ball exists at that position.

The 2D layout is intentionally formatted to visually match the physical package outline:
  Standard grid:  each row has `columns` string entries.
  Alternating:    staggered rows use a leading or trailing null to show the physical offset.
  Partial rows:   null entries mark absent ball positions within a row.

Example — 5×3 WLCSP with alternating_type 1 (middle row staggered right):
  [ ["OVSS", "VON",  "AVIN",  "AGND",  "SWIRE" ],
    [ null,  "LX1",  "PVIN",  "SET",   "ENA"   ],
    ["PGND", "LX2",  "VOP",   "OVDD",  "AVDD"  ] ]

oneOf.description: Signal name of the ball at this position.

display.description: Rendering and label display preferences for the Visio drawing.

show_designator_inside.description: Show the ball designator (e.g. A1) inside the ball circle.

show_designator_outside.description: Show the ball designator outside the ball circle.

show_pin_name.description: Show the signal name next to the ball.

pin_font_size.description: Base font size for pin name labels.
